text:
alex: Heads up — seeing sporadic RX errors and micro-flaps on a small subset of c6gn boxes after the ena driver + kernel bump we pushed at 09:20 UTC. East-west RPCs to model shards are timing out intermittently.

maria: Which counters are spiking? MTU changes, or something else?

alex: Quick snapshot from one affected host (eth0):
```
ethtool -S eth0 | egrep 'rx|tx|drop|error'
rx_packets: 12345678
rx_errors: 482
rx_dropped: 0
rx_over_errors: 0
rx_crc_errors: 0
rx_nohandler: 174
tx_packets: 8765432
tx_errors: 0
```
Not huge errors overall but correlated with short (200-800ms) link flaps visible in dmesg: `ENA 0: lost link to hw, reset` and then a quick carry-on.

james: How many hosts? Are they all in the same AZ / NIC firmware batch? Could be coalesce settings interacting with jumbo MTU + bursty RDMA-like traffic.

alex: ~6 hosts across two racks in us-west-2a, same image build, same ena fw 2.3.4. Kernel 6.1. Coalesce usecs set to 2000 for throughput tuning. MTU 9000.

maria: Can you try toggling GRO/LRO and reducing rx_coalesce_usecs as a quick canary? Those have bitten us before with the ena + bursty IPC pattern.

alex: Yep running these on one canary now:
```bash
sudo ethtool -K eth0 gro off lro off
sudo ethtool -C eth0 rx-usecs 200
# also testing MTU 8972 as a middle ground
sudo ip link set dev eth0 mtu 8972
```
Will throttle traffic to the shard and watch for flaps.

ops-oncall: I'm going to cordon one of the affected nodes and move live pods off it. Can we get a tcpdump during the next flap window? Use capture filter `host 10.0.12.34 and port 9100` and ring it to the thread.

alex: Captured a short pcap and dmesg snippet — attaching to ticket. The tcpdump shows bursts of retransmits followed by immediate recovery. dmesg shows repeated `ena: reset device` right before application timeouts.

maria: If coalesce reduction and GRO/LRO off stabilizes it, that's a good mitigation. We should also try switching ena driver back to previous release on a canary to determine whether it was the kernel/ena bump or firmware interaction.

james: Agreed. Also check `ethtool -k eth0` for offloads (rx/tx-checksumming, scatter-gather). Sometimes offload combos + MTU 9000 + long coalesce create fragmentation edge cases.

alex: `ethtool -k` shows rx-checksumming: on, tx-checksumming: on, scatter-gather: on. Turning rx-checksumming off temporarily now.

infra-bot: Incident INC-2024-5239 created and linked to this thread (priority P2).

ops-oncall: Rolling back ena package on two canaries to the previous kernel-driver build (k6.0-ena2.2) now, will watch for recurrences for 30m. If rollback removes flaps, we'll schedule a staged rollback.

alex: After coalesce -> 200 and GRO/LRO off + mtu 8972, the canary ran stable for 45m with zero RX errors. Rolling one more node into test.

maria: Good. Let's prepare a postmortem checklist: how many instances, fw versions, exact driver+kernel, coalesce settings, and build a cluster-wide probe to detect these micro-flaps (simple HTTP healthchecks timed at 100ms resolution). Also consider defaulting coalesce to 500 on c6gn family until we have a root cause.

james: I'll open an ops PR to add the probe and a runbook entry for ENA micro-flaps.

alex: Dumping the final canary config and pcap link into the ticket. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
